statement: The NDC reports Pakistan contributes about 0.9% of global GHG emissions yet is highly climate-vulnerable, citing floods, rainfall shifts, glacier melt, and vector-borne disease.
compact_statement: The NDC reports Pakistan contributes about 0.9% of global GHG emissions yet is highly climate-vulnerable, citing floods, rainfall shifts, glacier melt, and vector-borne disease.

source_refs.locator: NDC climate vulnerability trends, PDF p. 22; printed p. 22.

uncertainty: This is the government’s national synthesis, not a new vulnerability ranking produced in this extraction.

statement: The NDC describes GLOF risk in the upper Indus; storms and seawater intrusion on the Balochistan and Sindh coasts; river floods and agricultural heat in Punjab and Sindh; and aridity across parts of Punjab, Sindh, and Balochistan.
compact_statement: The NDC describes GLOF risk in the upper Indus; storms and seawater intrusion on the Balochistan and Sindh coasts; river floods and agricultural heat in Punjab and Sindh; and aridity across parts of Punjab, Sindh, and Balochistan.

source_refs.locator: NDC climate impact drivers, PDF p. 23; printed p. 23.

uncertainty: Regional patterns are the NDC’s summary and are not district-level hazard estimates.

statement: The NDC cites moderate or severe food insecurity among 40% of households in FY2020 as limiting capacity to absorb further climate shocks.
compact_statement: The NDC cites moderate or severe food insecurity among 40% of households in FY2020 as limiting capacity to absorb further climate shocks.

source_refs.locator: NDC climate vulnerability trends, PDF p. 22; printed p. 22.

uncertainty: The statistic is for FY2020 and should not be read as a current estimate.

statement: The NDC identifies agriculture as highly affected by climate variability and reports that it accounts for 95% of national freshwater withdrawals.
compact_statement: The NDC identifies agriculture as highly affected by climate variability and reports that it accounts for 95% of national freshwater withdrawals.

source_refs.locator: NDC adaptation policy initiatives, PDF pp. 38–39; printed pp. 38–39.

uncertainty: The water-withdrawal share is a national NDC estimate; this passage does not disaggregate it by province.

statement: The PDNA reports 2022 floods affected 33 million people, displaced nearly 8 million, and killed over 1,700; 94 districts were calamity-hit by October 11.
compact_statement: The PDNA reports 2022 floods affected 33 million people, displaced nearly 8 million, and killed over 1,700; 94 districts were calamity-hit by October 11.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, PDF p. 13 (printed p. 2), with district count as of October 11, 2022, PDF p. 14 (printed p. 3).

uncertainty: Rapid preliminary estimates during an ongoing disaster.

statement: The PDNA estimates US$14.9 billion damage, US$15.2 billion losses, and US$16.3 billion recovery needs; housing, agriculture, and transport were hardest hit.
compact_statement: The PDNA estimates US$14.9 billion damage, US$15.2 billion losses, and US$16.3 billion recovery needs; housing, agriculture, and transport were hardest hit.
uncertainty: Rounded rapid-assessment estimates; see source caveat.

statement: The PDNA estimates 780,000 houses destroyed and 1.27 million partly damaged; Sindh accounted for 83% of housing damage.
compact_statement: The PDNA estimates 780,000 houses destroyed and 1.27 million partly damaged; Sindh accounted for 83% of housing damage.

source_refs.locator: Housing sector assessment, PDF p. 53 (printed p. 52).

uncertainty: Preliminary estimates; some areas were inaccessible.

statement: The PDNA estimates flood-related poverty rose 3.7–4.0 percentage points (8.4–9.1 million people) and multidimensional poverty 5.9 points.
compact_statement: The PDNA estimates flood-related poverty rose 3.7–4.0 percentage points (8.4–9.1 million people) and multidimensional poverty 5.9 points.
scenario: Preliminary short-term flood-impact estimate; relief and recovery design may change outcomes.

source_refs.locator: Human Impact Assessment, PDF pp. 47–48 (printed pp. 46–47).

uncertainty: Preliminary estimates; results vary by location and recovery design.

statement: Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy says declining groundwater, recurring drought and heatwaves erode agriculture and displace vulnerable, resource-dependent rural communities, increasing poverty in Balochistan.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy says declining groundwater, recurring drought and heatwaves erode agriculture and displace vulnerable, resource-dependent rural communities, increasing poverty in Balochistan.
uncertainty: Provincial policy framing; it does not quantify these pathways by district.

statement: Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy reports that rain-induced floods displaced over 1.3 million people in Balochistan in 2022; women, youth and vulnerable communities face disproportionate climate-related food and health risks.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy reports that rain-induced floods displaced over 1.3 million people in Balochistan in 2022; women, youth and vulnerable communities face disproportionate climate-related food and health risks.
uncertainty: The policy gives a province-wide 2022 displacement figure without district breakdown.

statement: Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy says climate disasters combined with social norms obstruct women's access to healthcare, including transport, supplies, skilled staff and information.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-11-19 reports: The policy says climate disasters combined with social norms obstruct women's access to healthcare, including transport, supplies, skilled staff and information.
uncertainty: The passage describes provincial barriers but does not quantify service access by district.

statement: Source dated 2025-07-25 reports: As of 25 July 2025, NDMA reported 266 deaths and 628 injuries from heavy rain and flash floods since 26 June; reported deaths included 144 in Punjab, 63 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 25 in Sindh and 16 in Balochistan.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-07-25 reports: As of 25 July 2025, NDMA reported 266 deaths and 628 injuries from heavy rain and flash floods since 26 June; reported deaths included 144 in Punjab, 63 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 25 in Sindh and 16 in Balochistan.
uncertainty: Dated situation totals during an ongoing monsoon season; not a final event tally.

statement: Source dated 2025-07-25 reports: By 25 July 2025, health contingency plans and high-risk district control rooms were activated, medical supplies prepositioned, and partner mobile units had served over 3,000 people in Rawalpindi, Chakwal, Attock, Sargodha, Sohbatpur and Usta Muhammad.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-07-25 reports: By 25 July 2025, health contingency plans and high-risk district control rooms were activated, medical supplies prepositioned, and partner mobile units had served over 3,000 people in Rawalpindi, Chakwal, Attock, Sargodha, Sohbatpur and Usta Muhammad.
uncertainty: The report gives operational outputs, not independent outcome or coverage evaluation.

statement: IPC's February 2026 analysis classified food insecurity for December 2025–March 2026 across 45 rural districts, citing weather shocks and localized insecurity among several drivers.
compact_statement: IPC's February 2026 analysis classified food insecurity for December 2025–March 2026 across 45 rural districts, citing weather shocks and localized insecurity among several drivers.
affected_groups: people classified in IPC Phase 3 or worse
uncertainty: Classification-period estimate informed by September–November 2025 survey and secondary data; not observed outcomes for every month or an October 2026 caseload.

statement: Source dated 2026-02-18 reports: IPC identifies localized insecurity as a main food-insecurity driver in Kachi and Tank, disrupting livelihoods, markets, services and income.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-02-18 reports: IPC identifies localized insecurity as a main food-insecurity driver in Kachi and Tank, disrupting livelihoods, markets, services and income.

source_refs.locator: Drivers and district findings, PDF pp. 2 and 6.

uncertainty: The report describes insecurity as a food-insecurity driver, not as caused by climate hazards.

statement: Source dated 2026-02-18 reports: The household assessment associated drought with income declines of 30% in Balochistan, 14% in Sindh and 9% in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; respondents also reported water scarcity and reduced crop or livestock production.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-02-18 reports: The household assessment associated drought with income declines of 30% in Balochistan, 14% in Sindh and 9% in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; respondents also reported water scarcity and reduced crop or livestock production.
uncertainty: Self-reported survey livelihood/income associations in the assessment period, not a causally attributed climate effect or current provincial income loss.
